column1: # planning/fidelity/readme.pairing.tsv — which build node answers which mock affordance.
# Four tab-separated columns:  state <TAB> affordance <TAB> node <TAB> citation
# This file declares ONLY the pairing. `present`, `divergent`, `absent` and `unclassified` are
# computed by scripts/acceptance/mock_fidelity.py from the two artifacts on every run, which is
# what makes `present` earned by measuring rather than asserted. Deleting a line here does not
# delete a row from the ledger: the mock side is derived from the mock every run, so an affordance
# with no line becomes `absent`, which is a finding.
#   node = -            the affordance has no counterpart in this run
#   affordance = +path  a BUILD node with no mock peer, and the citation saying why
# EVERY CITATION OPENS WITH `Dn · `, naming the divergence in readme.layers.json it falls under —
# settings.pairing.tsv's rule, adopted here for its reason: an allowance list that does not
# adjudicate its own findings teaches the next reader that it is not authoritative. The numbers
# reach the generated ledger's citation column, so the split is countable off the run's own
# artifact rather than off this file.
# THE SINGLE FACT THAT DECIDES MOST OF THIS FILE: the mock keeps the read me, the changelog and the
# capability list in the DOM at once and toggles `hidden`, so the census inventories all three; a
# tab renders one. Twenty-four rows below are the changelog's and the capability list's, and every
